nodes.label: Audit policy v0.1
nodes.rationale: Spec 05 §7–§10. Values are placeholders the spec says live in config. Changing them changes future sampling decisions but never past ones, because each past decision is stored with its inputs in audit_schedules — the policy is versioned (policy_version audit-policy-v0.1) so a sampling decision stays reproducible after the config moves.

nodes.label: independent_checks (three independent answers)
nodes.rationale: Owner request, 2026-09-19. A claim's verification tasks ask for three independent answers. The first answer counts at once so one assistant can carry its own work through to something postable; the remaining two are what actually raise confidence, and the task stays open until they arrive or nobody comes. Trades immediate usefulness against corroboration without blocking the first contributor.

nodes.label: Audit sampling factors
nodes.rationale: base_rate 0.10 raised by multipliers: a new identity (first 10 contributions) by 5, low reliability (mean below 0.8) by 2, unusual activity by 2, and impact divided by 5. Sampling is risk-weighted rather than uniform.

nodes.label: anonymous_factor (ANONYMOUS principals sampled more)
nodes.rationale: Stage 12. Contributions whose principal is ANONYMOUS are sampled 3x more often. Anonymous contribution is permitted rather than blocked, and the cost of that openness is paid in audit rate instead of in refusal.

nodes.label: High-impact confirming-audit bands
nodes.rationale: Spec 05 §10. How many confirming audits from distinct principals are needed before provisional clears, banded by downstream_count: 1 audit up to 2 downstream, 2 up to 9, and above that 2 audits plus an accepted OPPOSING_EVIDENCE_SEARCH (Stage 8). The more other claims depend on it, the more it costs to stop being provisional, and at the top band someone must have actively looked for the contrary case.

nodes.label: Auditor eligibility and domains
nodes.rationale: An auditor needs at least 5 audits and a mean of 0.8; established tiers are ESTABLISHED, EXTERNALLY_VERIFIED and INSTITUTIONAL. Reputation is domain-specific: general, ancient_near_east, us_economics, defaulting to general.
